:::{#def-frobenius-norm}
#### Frobenius norm

The **Frobenius norm** of an $n \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ is

$$
\norm{\matr{A}}_F \eqdef \sqrt{\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{A}}}
$$

where $\iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}$ is the matrix inner product
(@def-matrix-inner-product).

:::

::: notes
By @thm-matrix-inner-product-entries,
$\norm{\matr{A}}_F^2 = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sum_{j=1}^{p} a_{ij}^2$,
a sum of squares, so the square root is always defined.
$\norm{\matr{A}}_F$ is the Euclidean norm (@def-euclidean-norm)
of the entries of $\matr{A}$, listed as one vector of length $np$
[@banerjee2014linear, Chapter 15, Definition 15.4, p. 492].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-frobenius-norm}
#### The Frobenius norm of a $2 \times 2$ matrix

For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$:

$$
\ba
\norm{\matr{A}}_F
&= \sqrt{\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{A}}}
&& \text{(definition of the Frobenius norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 2 + 3 \cd 3 + 4 \cd 4}
&& \text{(sum of products of matching entries)}
\\
&= \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9 + 16}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= \sqrt{30}
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

The second step is @thm-matrix-inner-product-entries.

:::
